title: Tokenization overhead vs context length — scratchpad
content:
Goal:
Quickly quantify how tokenization cost (CPU + wall time) scales with different request context lengths and payload shapes, and how that contributes to overall tail latencies on the hosted stack prototype (g4dn-like nodes).

Motivation / hypothesis:
- We often attribute short-request tail latency to model exec and KV cache warmups; tokenizer cost can be non-negligible when requests are many small strings.
- Hypothesis: per-request tokenization overhead is roughly linear with input bytes but shows fixed-cost startup (~polylog) and a second-order effect for many short segments (tokenizer overhead per segment).

Experiment setup (quick):
- Machine: ci-bench-node-07 (8vCPU, 32GB, g4dn-like). Python 3.10, tokenizers v0.13, Rust-backed BPE.
- Workload harness: local runner calling fasttokenize.py (micro-bench) to isolate tokenization only, and full-stack replay stress to measure end-to-end.
- Commands used:
  - python fasttokenize.py --model gpt-3-style --batch 1 --requests 10000 --context "short" --segments 1
  - python fasttokenize.py --model gpt-3-style --batch 8 --requests 2000 --context "long" --segments 10
  - replay tool: infra/replay --trace=small_chat.trace --concurrency=60 --tokenize-only=false --measure=latency

Test vectors (representative):
- short-single: 1–8 chars (user pings), 1 segment
- short-multi: 1–8 chars, 8 segments (many short fields)
- mid: 100–512 chars single segment
- long: 1k–4k chars single segment
- very-long: 8k–16k chars (payloads that exceed typical KV cache slice)

Micro-bench results (tokenization-only; median / p50 in microseconds, 1k requests per vector):
- short-single: p50 420us, p95 1.1ms, mean 510us
- short-multi (8 seg): p50 1.6ms, p95 4.2ms, mean 1.9ms
- mid: p50 1.3ms, p95 2.5ms, mean 1.4ms
- long: p50 3.6ms, p95 6.9ms, mean 3.8ms
- very-long: p50 9.8ms, p95 18.2ms, mean 10.5ms

Observations from micro-bench:
- Overhead is not strictly linear with bytes; per-segment overhead causes short-multi to cost more than a single mid-sized segment with similar total bytes.
- p95 grows faster than median as length increases (expected due to allocator/cache effects).
- Single-request tokenization for tiny inputs still ~400us — non-trivial when target end-to-end SLO is 20ms for short chats.

End-to-end replay notes (replay with model forward):
- Replayed small_chat.trace (mix of short-single and short-multi). Measured p50/p95 end-to-end: 18ms / 96ms.
- Replayed mid-heavy.trace: p50/p95: 37ms / 152ms.
- With tokenize-only flag on (server-side tokenization disabled, pre-tokenized client trace) p95 improved by ~12–18ms on small_chat.trace.

Implications for platform routing and batching:
- For workloads dominated by short-multi (many fields), pre-tokenization on client (or edge) yields larger wins than for long monolithic contexts.
- Batching at server (batch size 8–16) amortizes model execution but does not reduce tokenizer overhead unless server can merge tokenization for batched parallel requests (unlikely without rework).

Quick ASCII chart (median tokenization time vs payload size):
bytes | median(us)
------------------
16    | 420
64    | 480
256   | 1300
1024  | 3600
8192  | 9800

Anomalies / noise noted:
- Several runs showed 2–6x p95 spikes correlated with system GC and background backup cron at 02:00+ local — re-run windows should avoid backup windows.
- One outlier long-run had a rust tokenizer fallback to Python in logs (race on binary wheel) — need to pin tokenizer wheel in CI.

Actionable next steps (short list):
- Add a dedicated micro-bench in perf-suite to capture "many short segments" pattern; add to CI smoke to catch wheel fallbacks.
- Experiment: server-side tokenization pool (pinned threads) vs current per-request Python worker to see if p95 improves for short-multi.
- Evaluate shipping pre-tokenization in SDK for latency-sensitive routes (opt-in).
- File infra ticket to pin tokenizers wheel build on all runner images (linked_artifacts: GH PR).

Open questions / TODO:
- How much memory pressure does pre-tokenization add for very-long contexts at high concurrency? Need a memory/cost sweep.
- Could we create a lightweight C ABI shim for tokenization to avoid Python process overhead? (research + feasibility).
- If payloads are many tiny segments, could the client pack segments into a single string with separators to reduce per-segment overhead without changing semantics? Try 3 examples.

Notes-to-self:
- Re-run short-multi with batch=16 and controlled CPU affinity to isolate contention.
- Add p99 to micro-bench reporting.

Raw commands & quick knobs (copyable):
- python -m bench.tokenize --pattern short-single --n 20000 --workers 4 --json out_short_single.json
- infra/replay --trace=small_chat.trace --concurrency=80 --warmup=30 --duration=120 --pretokenize=true --out=replay_pretok_small.json

Conclusion (quick):
Tokenization adds a measurable floor to short-request latencies, especially when requests contain many tiny segments. For latency SLOs < 50ms, we should treat tokenization as a first-class optimization target: pin the tokenizer wheel, consider client-side opt-in pre-tokenization, and prototype a server-side pooled tokenizer to reduce p95 spikes.

-- Antoine
